ss-delta 0.5.2 fixes square blocks in smoke, fire and fog on graphics cards whose driver lacks two features the effects rely on (older AMD Radeon such as the R5 APUs, and Qualcomm's own Adreno driver on Android). Ad Hoc Play now also works over the internet, through a VPN such as Tailscale, ZeroTier or Radmin VPN. On Android, the game's files install on phones that refused them (a Galaxy S25). The log now also names the graphics cards and the network adapter the game uses, to help with laptops that start on the wrong card and with LAN play that doesn't connect.

## Downloads

| System | Download | Start |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11, x64 | `ss-delta-v0.5.2-windows.zip` | `ss-delta.exe` |
| Linux x64, Steam Deck | `ss-delta-v0.5.2-linux.tar.gz` | `ss-delta.x86_64` |
| macOS 13.3+ on Apple Silicon | `ss-delta-v0.5.2-macos.tar.gz` | `Soul Sacrifice Delta.app` |
| Android 9+, 64-bit ARM with Vulkan | `ss-delta-v0.5.2-android.apk` | **ss-delta** (install the APK) |

On a PC, unpack the archive and start the game. The first time, its importer asks for your own dump of Soul Sacrifice Delta (US PCSA00152 or EU PCSF00532, update 1.30), downloads the PS Vita firmware from Sony (about 180 MB; the compiler is in the download), and builds the game on your computer in a few minutes. From then on the program goes straight to the game. Nothing of the game is in these downloads. See the [installation guide](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md).

macOS: the app isn't signed by a registered Apple developer, so macOS refuses it the first time. Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click "Open Anyway".

## Fixed

* **Android: the game's files wouldn't install on some phones** ([#23](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/23)), such as a Galaxy S25: the setup stopped at "Failed to load archive file". The app now reads the files you pick through the access Android's file picker gives it, instead of opening them again by name, which those phones refuse to an app without storage permission.
* **Building the Android app's game from Windows** (`--android`) stopped with `relocation R_AARCH64_ABS64 cannot be used against symbol ...; recompile with -fPIC` since 0.5.0 ([#23](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/23)).
* **Square blocks in smoke, fire and fog on some graphics cards** ([#17](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/17)). On cards whose driver has neither shader interlock nor raster-order attachment access (the log's `Framebuffer reads:` line says "no, no"), the effects' shaders now leave their blending to the graphics card's own blender instead of reading the picture, and look as on other cards. Other cards draw exactly as before. `[debug] shader_blend` on the settings menu's Debug page turns this off if something looks wrong on your card.

## New

* **Ad Hoc Play over the internet**, through a VPN (Tailscale, ZeroTier, Radmin VPN or another) or between subnets, where broadcasts don't arrive: the other players type the host's VPN address into **Peers (host address)** on the settings menu's Multiplayer page. Step by step: [Playing together over the internet](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/ONLINE-PLAY.md).
* **Typing in the settings menu**: Peers takes a keyboard (Android's on-screen one too) or a gamepad (Up/Down change the character under the cursor).
* **Network adapter `auto`** (the new default) takes the adapter that reaches the first peer, or the one of the internet connection, not a virtual adapter that Windows lists first (Hyper-V, WSL).
* **The log lists every graphics card** Vulkan offers the game, and `[debug] gpu` picks one by its number there (for a laptop that starts on the wrong one).
* **Ad Hoc Play over LAN: the log names the network adapter** the game uses, with its address, and lists the others ([#21](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/21)). Windows often lists a virtual adapter first (vEthernet, Hyper-V, VPN); pick your home network's on the settings menu's Multiplayer page (Network adapter), and allow `ss-delta.exe` through the firewall on private and public networks. `[debug] net_trace` logs every Ad Hoc packet, for a connection that doesn't work.

## Upgrading from 0.5.0 or 0.5.1

No new build is needed: the game's recompiled code is the same as in 0.5.0. Unpack 0.5.2 over your game's folder (replace the files) and start it; saves and settings are kept. RecompLauncher builds the game again after the update by itself, as for every release. Coming from 0.4.x, build again with `--install` (see the [0.5.0 notes](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/releases/tag/v0.5.0)); from 0.3 or older, see [Updating](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md#updating).

Players of Ad Hoc Play should all use the same release.

Every release's changes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

SHA-256 and build attestations: see the files attached, and `gh attestation verify`.
